name: New York City (Con Edison)
summary: NYC (Con Edison, NYISO Zone J) is one of the highest-value US markets for BTM C&I storage on paper. Stacked value comes from: very high, multi-window SC 9 Rate II demand charges (2026-2028 rate plan adopted 2026-01-22); Zone J capacity, which cleared at a record $32.6/kW-month in May 2026 and $32.5 in June 2026; Con Ed CSRP ($18/kW-month outside Staten Island) and DLRP ($18/$25 per kW-month by network tier) reservation payments; and the NYSERDA retail incentive (NYC block proposed at $125/kWh). Capacity is softening: the 1,250 MW CHPE line entered the July 2026 auction, so post-June 2026 Zone J prices and capacity-tag value should be modeled lower. Tag savings reach the customer only if the retail supply contract passes them through. The binding constraints are physical and regulatory, not economic. Most of Manhattan and much of the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens is fed by secondary area or spot networks, so systems must be non-export: network protectors trip on reverse power, and Con Ed flags systems above 50 kW-AC. FDNY rules come next. Every unit model needs an FDNY Certificate of Approval. Outdoor systems above 250 kWh are 'Large' under 3 RCNY 608-01, with 10 ft separation from lot lines and exposures. Indoor lithium-ion is reportedly capped at 400 kWh per control area under the 2022 NYC Fire Code. As a result, the 418 kWh and 600 kWh units are effectively outdoor or rooftop products in NYC, while the 150 kWh and 200 kWh units are the indoor and basement candidates. Current 2026 SC 9 $/kW values, the Jul–Oct 2026 Zone J prices and the Term/Auto-DLM prices were not verifiable in this pass (search-only environment) and are null.

utilities.name: Consolidated Edison Company of New York (Con Edison), NYC service area
utilities.load_zone: Zone J (New York City). Westchester (also Con Ed) sits outside Zone J and is not in scope.
utilities.default_supply_notes: Full-service customers pay Con Ed's Market Supply Charge (MSC), which resets monthly and includes a capacity component. For SC 9 Rates II and V, the MSC capacity component is a $/kW charge: $9.99/kW in NYC in the March 2025 statement (msccap-202503). The capacity statement is republished monthly (e.g., msccap-202605). The basis kW (billing demand vs capacity tag) was not confirmed. Large customers are believed to be on mandatory day-ahead hourly supply pricing; the kW threshold is unverified. ESCO supply is available, and capacity/ICAP tag savings flow only if the ESCO contract passes capacity through at the customer's tag.
utilities.network_grid_notes: Much of NYC (Manhattan and large parts of the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens) is served by low-voltage secondary area networks, and large buildings may sit on dedicated spot networks. Network protectors open when power flows back from the LV bus toward the feeder, which is the same condition as an ESS discharging more than the local load. Con Ed flags undesirable impacts (voltage fluctuation, repetitive network protector operation), particularly for ESS above 50 kW-AC. In practice BTM storage in network areas must be non-export, with a minimum-import margin. Staten Island (and Westchester) are largely radial, which is why CSRP pays a lower reservation rate there.

interconnection.rule_name: NYS Standardized Interconnection Requirements (SIR) for DG and energy storage <=5 MW. The version in effect is effective 2026-02-09 (Case 24-E-0621 redline of the 2025-08-01 SIR). Con Ed also publishes an Energy Storage System Guide (v4, July 2022) and ESS Interconnection Best Practices.

tracks.name: Simplified / expedited (small inverter-based)
tracks.conditions: Inverter-based systems up to 50 kW. The 50 kW boundary follows the SIR structure as commonly applied. It was not re-confirmed from the 2026 SIR text in this pass.

tracks.name: Standard process
tracks.conditions: Systems above 50 kW up to 5 MW AC nameplate or export capacity. Includes preliminary/supplemental screening and CESIR (coordinated electric system interconnection review) where screens fail. Energy storage applications include the AC inverter/converter nameplate. Export is capped at 5 MW AC.

interconnection.non_export_path: Under the 2025 SIR edits, UL 1741 CRD (Certification Requirement Decision) Power Control Systems with multi-mode capability can limit export or import, so a non-export or limited-export ESS can be evaluated at its controlled export level rather than inverter nameplate. In Con Ed networks, non-export is effectively mandatory. Expect a reverse-power or minimum-import relay at the PCC, coordinated with network protector settings, and Con Ed protection review for anything above 50 kW-AC.
interconnection.storage_specific_notes: Con Ed filed a 'Notice on SIR Energy Storage' with DPS on 2026-01-14 (content not retrieved). On 2025-08-15, Con Ed told developers about capacity constraints at specific substations and said projects without executed interconnection agreements need further evaluation. Check substation and network headroom before committing sites. Grid charging adds load and can trigger service or transformer upgrades even when export is zero.

demand_charges.label: MSC capacity component (full-service supply only)
demand_charges.notes: Con Ed bills SC 9 Rates II and V supply capacity in $/kW: $9.99/kW NYC in March 2025 (a winter month). Summer 2026 statements should be far higher given $32+/kW-month Zone J prices. The kW basis is not confirmed. It does not apply to ESCO customers.

coincident_peak_charges.how_set: Customer capacity obligation (ICAP tag) is set from the customer's load at the prior summer's peak, NYISO/Con Ed peak hour. The exact Con Ed methodology (NYCA vs Con Ed zonal peak, scaling to the Zone J Locational Capacity Requirement and UCAP) was not verified. The tag applies to the following May-April capability year.
coincident_peak_charges.derivation: Inputs (UCAP spot, Zone J): May 2026 $32.6, June 2026 $32.5/kW-month. Jul-Oct 2026 are unknown (CHPE 1,250 MW entered the July auction, so prices are expected lower). Winter 2025-26 was roughly $6/kW-month. Known-to-date summer 2026 sum: 32.6 + 32.5 = $65.1/kW. Upper-bound scenario if all 6 summer months held May/June levels: 6 x 32.55 = 195.3, plus winter 6 x ~6 = 36, for about $231/kW-yr before any tag-to-UCAP scaling (Zone J LCR and derating factors, roughly ±20%). This is not a central estimate. A tag reduction earned in summer 2026 is priced in capability year 2027-28, which is post-CHPE and likely materially lower. Left null pending NYISO auction results for Jul-Oct 2026 and the 2026-27 winter strip.
coincident_peak_charges.passthrough_notes: Realized only if (a) the customer is full-service on the MSC, where the capacity $/kW tracks the tag or demand basis (verify), or (b) the ESCO contract is capacity pass-through or index at the customer's tag. Fixed all-in ESCO contracts capture none of it until renewal.

tariffs.storage_notes: Rate II's overlapping windows mean a 2-4 h battery shaves the monthly peak within each window, not the whole 14-hour 8am-10pm block. Each window's charge is assessed on that window's own monthly max, so one dispatch reduces several charges at once. Charging must be power-limited to avoid setting the all-hours peak. Standby (SC 14-RA) applicability to storage-only customers was not verified (see coned-sc14ra). Non-export applies in network areas.

programs.name: Con Edison Commercial System Relief Program (CSRP), Rider T
programs.status_notes: 2026 Capability Period guidelines and application are published. Aggregators and direct participants must submit an application each capability period.

eligibility.other: Direct enrollment or via aggregator. The 50 kW minimum is verified for DLRP and assumed the same for CSRP (verify). Each customer can take Reservation OR Voluntary for each program, and can be in CSRP and DLRP concurrently.

valuation.kw_basis: pledged/committed kW verified by performance in events (performance factor)
valuation.notes: Annual reservation value in Manhattan, Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens = $18 x 5 = $90/kW-yr (5 months assumes a May-Sep capability period, which is standard Rider T practice but not re-verified). Deliverable kW = min(kW, kWh/4): 30/150 -> 30 kW, 65/200 -> 50 kW, 200/418 -> 104.5 kW, 200/600 -> 150 kW. Reservation payments are scaled by event performance. One snippet mentioned month-based adjustments ($6 vs $11/kW-month for months with ≤4 vs ≥5 planned events); that is unclear, so verify in the Rider T guidelines.

dispatch.window: 4-hour call window on weekdays (excluding holidays), fixed by network: 11am-3pm, 2pm-6pm, 4pm-8pm or 7pm-11pm. Several networks were reassigned for 2025; confirm with the Network Lookup tool in the DR/SUR portal.
dispatch.notice: 21-hour (day-ahead) for planned events. Triggered when the day-ahead forecast is ≥92% of the forecast summer peak. Unplanned events also exist.
dispatch.baseline_or_mv: Customer baseline load (CBL) per Rider T guidelines, interval metering
dispatch.event_block_notes: Default 2pm-6pm when the site's network window is not set. Pick the network's window in the screener (Rates & programs).

stacking.notes: CSRP and DLRP concurrent enrollment is allowed (one option per program). SCR dual participation is commonly done but should be verified in the 2026 guidelines. CSRP afternoon windows overlap SC 9 Rate II peak windows, so dispatch helps both. Conflicts as researched: coned-term-dlm and coned-auto-dlm, for the same kW (likely; verify)

programs.vpp_relevance: The core NYC VPP revenue. Aggregators can pool sites at or above the minimum and manage performance factor across a portfolio. The network-tier map drives value by site.

site_constraints.title: FDNY Certificate of Approval required for each ESS unit
site_constraints.rule: Every ESS/battery unit must hold an FDNY Certificate of Approval (COA) to be eligible for plan review and installation approval. Outdoor units of 2 kWh or less are exempt.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Gates product selection. If the specific 150/200/418/600 kWh product SKU lacks an FDNY COA, it cannot be installed in NYC regardless of size. Check the FDNY COA list first.

site_constraints.title: FDNY permit for outdoor ESS above 20 kWh; all indoor ESS permitted
site_constraints.rule: Outdoor systems with aggregate capacity above 20 kWh must be inspected and permitted by FDNY. All indoor ESS must be inspected and permitted by FDNY regardless of size. A DOB construction work permit is required for every stationary ESS regardless of size.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Every product in the lineup (smallest 150 kWh) triggers FDNY permit, inspection and DOB permit. Budget permitting time and cost for all sites.

site_constraints.title: FDNY 'Large' outdoor system (> 250 kWh): escalated requirements
site_constraints.rule: Outdoor lithium-ion systems are classed Small (>2 to ≤20 kWh), Medium (>20 to ≤250 kWh) and Large (>250 kWh). Requirements escalate by class.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: A single 418 kWh or 600 kWh unit is a 'Large' outdoor system. The 150 kWh and 200 kWh units are 'Medium' alone, but two or more aggregated likely exceed 250 kWh (aggregation and spacing rules need verification). Keeping aggregate outdoor capacity ≤250 kWh (e.g., 1 x 200 kWh) avoids Large-system requirements.

site_constraints.title: Indoor lithium-ion ESS maximum aggregate 400 kWh per control area (NYC FC 2022 section 608)
site_constraints.rule: The 2022 NYC Fire Code section 608 reportedly limits indoor lithium-ion ESS to 400 kWh aggregate per control area. The 600 kWh figure applies to lead-acid and nickel chemistries.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: A single 418 kWh or 600 kWh unit cannot fit indoors within one control area. Maximum indoor configurations per control area are 2 x 200 kWh (400 kWh) or 2 x 150 kWh (300 kWh). The 418/600 kWh units are outdoor or rooftop only unless FDNY approves otherwise.

site_constraints.title: Outdoor ESS 10 ft from lot lines and exposures
site_constraints.rule: Outdoor stationary storage battery systems must be at least 10 ft from lot lines and other exposures (buildings, egress, combustibles), unless the equipment or installation approval requires a different distance.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: On tight NYC lots this often rules out sidewalk-adjacent or yard placement. Rooftops or large parking lots may be the only outdoor options.

Rooftop installations must also demonstrate compliance with NYC FC 504.4 (rooftop access/clearances; the search summary tied this to roofs below 100 ft).
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Rooftop is the likely home for 418/600 kWh units. Structural load (multi-ton cabinets), crane logistics, FC 504.4 clearances and any rooftop kWh limit (not verified) cap the count per roof.

site_constraints.title: Con Ed secondary/spot networks: non-export with minimum import
site_constraints.rule: Network protectors open on reverse power, so an ESS discharging above site load trips protectors. Con Ed flags voltage and protector-cycling impacts especially for ESS above 50 kW-AC. Expect a non-export requirement, a reverse-power or minimum-import relay, and Con Ed review.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Discharge kW is capped at site load minus the import margin at every moment. Low-load periods (nights, weekends) cap usable discharge. Size inverter kW against the 15-minute minimum load during target windows, not nameplate. Above 50 kW-AC expect a longer, protection-focused review.
site_constraints.applies_to: coned-nyc (network areas: most of Manhattan and large parts of Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens)

panel_notes.note: Check the networks-and-tiers list before ranking sites. A Tier 2 network is worth $25/kW-month in DLRP versus $18 in Tier 1, and Staten Island earns only $6/kW-month in CSRP versus $18 elsewhere in NYC.

panel_notes.topic: CSRP plus DLRP on the same hot day
panel_notes.note: CSRP (11am-3pm or 2-6pm, day-ahead) and DLRP (any time 8am-midnight, 2-hour notice) can both be called on the same peak day. Dispatch logic must reserve energy after the CSRP window. A 200 kW/418 kWh unit that runs flat for 4 h at 104 kW in CSRP has nothing left for an evening DLRP call.
The 2026-2028 rate plan (adopted 2026-01-22) changed every delivery rate leaf. Pull the current SC 9 leaf rather than using older calculator libraries, because demand-window prices moved.

At $32+/kW-month in May/June 2026, the Zone J tag is a huge line item, but most C&I customers sit on fixed all-in ESCO contracts that won't credit a lower tag until renewal. Move hosts to a capacity pass-through product or the savings belong to the supplier.

Don't underwrite at the May 2026 record price. CHPE added 1,250 MW in Zone J from the July 2026 auction, and tag reductions earned this summer are priced in 2027-28. Run capacity at a haircut and treat the upside as merchant.

SCR enrollment is limited by the customer's ACL. If the battery has already shaved the peak hours that set the ACL and tag, you can't sell the same kW again as SCR. Pick one per kW and model it explicitly.
No FDNY Certificate of Approval for the exact product means no permit, whatever the site economics. Confirm COA status for all four SKUs before any site work, because COA review can take months.

Each 418/600 kWh unit is a 'Large' outdoor system under 3 RCNY 608-01 (>250 kWh) and exceeds the reported 400 kWh indoor lithium-ion limit per control area. Plan basements and indoor rooms around 150/200 kWh units, at no more than 2 x 200 kWh per control area, and verify that limit in FC 608.

The 10 ft setback from lot lines and exposures eliminates most NYC side yards and sidewalks. Rooftops need noncombustible roofing within 5 ft, FC 504.4 clearances and structural sign-off. Expect DOB plus FDNY permits on every site, even the smallest unit.

On spot or area networks, discharge must stay below instantaneous building load minus the import margin. Size inverter kW to the minimum load in the target windows from interval data, not to the peak, or protectors will cycle and Con Ed will force a derate.
SC 9 Rate II bills an all-hours demand component, so overnight charging at full 200 kW can set a new monthly all-hours peak. Enforce a site-level charge-power limit tied to the running monthly max.

The summer 8am-10pm window is 14 hours, so a 2.1 h unit (200/418) cannot flatten it. Value comes from clipping the monthly peak, which needs good load forecasting. The 3-5 h units (200/600, 30/150) suit the 4 h DR windows better.

Con Ed flags ESS above 50 kW-AC for network impact. Expect protection studies, a reverse-power relay and possibly CESIR for 200 kW units. Use UL 1741 CRD export limiting (accepted under the 2025 SIR edits) and file early, given the 2025 substation-constraint notice.

NYC storage property tax abatement: confirm current terms (30%/$250k over 4 yrs vs 10%/$62.5k per yr) and sunset under RPTL 499-bbbb, plus the status of 2025 bills A5959/S2470.
SIR simplified-track threshold (50 kW) and application fees in the 2026-02-09 SIR. Also the contents of Con Ed's 2026-01-14 SIR energy storage notice.

Confirm the 75% Tier-4 factor by reading the current PSC 10 SC 9 leaf directly. Derived standard SC 9 LT rates are: Rate II summer $12.31 (8a-6p), $24.79 (8a-10p), $22.39 (all hours); Rate II winter $21.35 (8a-10p), $6.43 (all hours); Rate I $48.67 summer, $39.27 winter. If Tier 4 were 100%, the EV Phase-In Tier 4 values themselves apply: $9.23/$18.59/$16.79/$16.01/$4.82 and $36.50/$29.45.

Add SC 9 Rate III (Voluntary Time-of-Day, about 10-1,500 kW) as a tariff. Rate II is mandatory only above 1,500 kW, so most hosts for 30-200 kW batteries sit on Rate I or Rate III. One snippet cited Rate III summer 8am-6pm charges up to $44.87/kW (vintage unknown).

Con Ed MSC capacity charge basis for SC 9 (msccap-2026xx): the summary indicates summer Mon-Fri 8am-6pm demand (Jun-Sep). If so, full-service customers capture capacity value through window peak-shaving each month, and the ICAP-tag passthrough mainly concerns ESCO customers. Read the msccap-202607/08/09 statements for the post-CHPE $/kW.

DLRP/CSRP: add the $5/kW-month reservation bonus after 5 or more events in a capability period to the program tiers or notes.
